cdc_milestone: Calms down when spoken to or picked up
question_text: Becomes calm when hearing voices they know.
match_reason: Same calming response to speech; Kinedu specifies familiar voices, one ordinary instance of CDC's spoken-to alternative.

cdc_milestone: Looks at your face
question_text: Stares at people's faces.
match_reason: Both describe looking at people's faces; no extra task or achievement threshold.

cdc_milestone: Smiles when you talk to or smile at her
question_text: Smiles when people make eye contact.
match_reason: Both describe an elicited social smile; Kinedu specifies eye contact rather than speech or an adult smile.

cdc_milestone: Reacts to loud sounds
question_text: Gets startled by loud sounds.
match_reason: Both describe a response to loud sounds; Kinedu specifies the startle response. This question has no numeric rate observations.

cdc_milestone: Watches you as you move
question_text: Turns their head to follow objects with their eyes.
match_reason: Same visual tracking of a moving target; CDC uses a person and Kinedu an object.

cdc_milestone: Holds head up when on tummy
question_text: When lying on their tummy, they lift their head for a short time.
match_reason: Both describe lifting/holding the head up while prone; CDC sets no longer duration requirement.

cdc_milestone: Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to get or keep your attention
question_text: Repeats sounds or actions to get people to look.
match_reason: Same use of sounds or actions to get attention; Kinedu describes repeating the attention bid.

cdc_milestone: Makes sounds like “oooo”, “aahh” (cooing)
question_text: Makes vowel sounds like 'eh' or 'ah'.
match_reason: Both describe open-vowel cooing, with equivalent ah/eh examples.

cdc_milestone: Looks at her hands with interest
question_text: Stares at their hands for a few seconds.
match_reason: Both describe looking at one's own hands for a short time.

cdc_milestone: Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
question_text: Grabs a small object placed in their hands.
match_reason: Both describe grasping/holding an object placed in the hand; Kinedu calls it a small object rather than a toy.

cdc_milestone: Brings hands to mouth
question_text: Brings their hands to their mouth.
match_reason: Same hand-to-mouth behavior.

cdc_milestone: Pushes up onto elbows/forearms when on tummy
question_text: Props up their upper body with their elbows and forearms when they're on their belly.
match_reason: Same prone upper-body support on elbows and forearms.

cdc_milestone: Knows familiar people
question_text: Recognizes caregivers.
match_reason: Same recognition of familiar people; Kinedu names the familiar caregivers.

cdc_milestone: Laughs
question_text: Laughs out loud.
match_reason: Same audible laugh; unlike CDC's earlier four-month chuckle, this item requires laughter.

cdc_milestone: Puts things in her mouth to explore them
question_text: Grabs objects and puts them in their mouth.
match_reason: Same exploration by putting objects in the mouth.

cdc_milestone: Reaches to grab a toy she wants
question_text: Reaches for something and grabs it.
match_reason: Both describe reaching for an object and grasping it.

cdc_milestone: Rolls from tummy to back
question_text: Rolls from tummy to back.
match_reason: Same tummy-to-back roll; not the harder roll-both-ways question.

cdc_milestone: Leans on hands to support herself when sitting
question_text: Uses their arms and hands to help them sit without falling over.
match_reason: Same hand/arm support to remain seated: supported or tripod sitting, not independent sitting.

cdc_milestone: Is shy, clingy, or fearful around strangers
question_text: Feels shy or anxious when meeting new adults.
match_reason: Both describe shyness or anxiety around unfamiliar adults.

cdc_milestone: Looks when you call her name
question_text: When they hear their name, they move toward the person by crawling, walking, or turning in their direction.
match_reason: Both include orienting when the child's name is called; Kinedu explicitly allows turning, so crawling/walking is not required.

cdc_milestone: Makes a lot of different sounds like “mamamama” and “bababababa”
question_text: Repeats 'baba' or 'dada' kind of sounds.
match_reason: Same repeated consonant-vowel babbling, with baba/dada equivalents to CDC's examples.

cdc_milestone: Lifts arms up to be picked up
question_text: Lifts their arms to be carried.
match_reason: Same raising the arms to be picked up/carried.

cdc_milestone: Looks for objects when dropped out of sight (like his spoon or toy)
question_text: Looks for an item they dropped on the floor.
match_reason: Same search for a dropped object; CDC explicitly says out of sight, while Kinedu says looking for the dropped item on the floor.

cdc_milestone: Bangs two things together
question_text: Hits two things together.
match_reason: Same banging/hitting two objects together.

cdc_milestone: Gets to a sitting position by herself
question_text: Goes from lying to sitting without help.
match_reason: Same independent transition into sitting from lying down.

cdc_milestone: Moves things from one hand to her other hand
question_text: Switches things between their hands.
match_reason: Same hand-to-hand object transfer.

cdc_milestone: Sits without support
question_text: Sits independently.
match_reason: Same unsupported, independent sitting.

cdc_milestone: Waves “bye-bye”
question_text: Says hello or goodbye with hand movements.
match_reason: Both include a conventional goodbye hand wave; Kinedu also permits the equivalent hello wave.

cdc_milestone: Calls a parent “mama” or “dada” or another special name
question_text: Refers to caregivers as 'mama' or 'papa.'
match_reason: Same meaningful name for a caregiver, with mama/papa examples.

cdc_milestone: Understands “no” (pauses briefly or stops when you say it)
question_text: Knows what 'no' means.
match_reason: Same understanding of the word no; Kinedu omits CDC's explanatory pause/stop example.

cdc_milestone: Puts something in a container, like a block in a cup
question_text: Puts things into containers.
match_reason: Same placing objects into a container.

cdc_milestone: Looks for things he sees you hide, like a toy under a blanket
question_text: Looks for a toy that was just hidden.
match_reason: Same search for a just-hidden toy; CDC makes watching the hiding explicit. Other hidden-toy questions are not counted again.

cdc_milestone: Pulls up to stand
question_text: Goes from sitting to standing with the aid of a large object, like furniture.
match_reason: Same supported transition to standing using furniture; Kinedu specifies a sitting start.

cdc_milestone: Walks, holding on to furniture
question_text: Walks or cruises while holding onto big furniture.
match_reason: Same cruising/walking while holding furniture.

cdc_milestone: Picks things up between thumb and pointer finger, like small bits of food
question_text: Holds small objects using their thumb and forefinger.
match_reason: Same thumb-and-index-finger pincer grasp; no numeric rate observations are available for this question.

cdc_milestone: Copies other children while playing, like taking toys out of a container when another child does
question_text: Imitates what friends do in play, such as building towers when they do.
match_reason: Same imitation of another child's actions during play; tower-building and taking toys out are examples, not added requirements.

cdc_milestone: Shows you affection (hugs, cuddles, or kisses you)
question_text: Expresses love to those familiar, like hugging them.
match_reason: Same affection toward familiar people, including hugging.

cdc_milestone: Looks at a familiar object when you name it
question_text: Looks at things or people when called by name.
match_reason: Same looking toward the named referent; Kinedu permits a named thing or person rather than only a familiar object.

cdc_milestone: Points to ask for something or to get help
question_text: Points to objects they want.
match_reason: Same pointing to request an object; CDC also permits a request for help.

cdc_milestone: Stacks at least two small objects, like blocks
question_text: Stacks two or more blocks to make a tower.
match_reason: Both set the same minimum of two stacked objects/blocks.

cdc_milestone: Takes a few steps on his own
question_text: Takes a couple of steps on their own.
match_reason: Same first few independent steps; not sustained walking.

cdc_milestone: Points to show you something interesting
question_text: Shows you things by pointing.
match_reason: Same declarative pointing to show another person something.

cdc_milestone: Helps you dress him by pushing arm through sleeve or lifting up foot
question_text: Helps with the dressing and undressing processes by moving the right body parts.
match_reason: Same active assistance with dressing by moving the appropriate body parts.

cdc_milestone: Plays with toys in a simple way, like pushing a toy car
question_text: Moves toys with wheels.
match_reason: Same simple functional toy play; moving a wheeled toy is CDC's pushing-a-car example.

cdc_milestone: Scribbles
question_text: Scribbles by moving their entire arm from the shoulder.
match_reason: Same early scribbling; Kinedu specifies the early whole-arm form, not later wrist-only drawing.

cdc_milestone: Says at least two words together, like “More milk.”
question_text: Puts two words together to make a brief phrase, like 'more cookie'.
match_reason: Same two-word combination, with equivalent more-cookie/more-milk examples.

cdc_milestone: Holds something in one hand while using the other hand; for example, holding a container and taking the lid off
question_text: Uses both hands together to manipulate objects, like opening a box.
match_reason: Same coordinated use of both hands to manipulate an object, illustrated by opening a box/container; Kinedu does not spell out each hand's role.

cdc_milestone: Tries to use switches, knobs, or buttons on a toy
question_text: Turns things that spin, like toy knobs or faucets.
match_reason: Both include turning toy knobs; Kinedu also permits turning a faucet.

cdc_milestone: Kicks a ball
question_text: Kicks a ball while standing.
match_reason: Same basic stationary ball kick, without added aiming, running or a moving target.

cdc_milestone: Eats with a spoon
question_text: Can use a spoon independently.
match_reason: Same functional independent eating with a spoon; not merely trying to use it.

cdc_milestone: Says about 50 words
question_text: Speaks around 50 words.
match_reason: Same approximate expressive vocabulary of 50 words.

cdc_milestone: Says two or more words together, with one action word, like “Doggie run”
question_text: Combines nouns and verbs, like 'mommy go'.
match_reason: Same two-word noun-plus-verb phrase, with mommy-go/doggie-run equivalents.

cdc_milestone: Says words like “I,” “me,” or “we”
question_text: Uses words like 'I,' 'me,' and 'you'.
match_reason: Same personal pronouns, with overlapping I/me examples.

cdc_milestone: Follows two-step instructions like “Put the toy down and close the door.”
question_text: Completes tasks with two steps, like 'Find your toy, bring it here.'
match_reason: Same two-step instruction. Both examples require two linked actions, even when Kinedu puts them in two short clauses.

cdc_milestone: Shows he knows at least one color, like pointing to a red crayon when you ask, “Which one is red?”
question_text: Points to a red object when you ask.
match_reason: Same requested pointing to a red object. Selecting red is one valid instance of knowing at least one color.

cdc_milestone: Uses hands to twist things, like turning doorknobs or unscrewing lids
question_text: Screws and unscrews a bottle cap.
match_reason: Same manual twisting to unscrew a lid; CDC gives unscrewing lids as an example.

cdc_milestone: Takes some clothes off by himself, like loose pants or an open jacket
question_text: Knows how to take off their shoes.
match_reason: Same independent removal of an item of clothing/attire; Kinedu uses shoes instead of CDC's loose-pants/open-jacket examples and specifies no fastener task.

cdc_milestone: Jumps off the ground with both feet
question_text: Jumps in place with both feet.
match_reason: Same two-footed jump up from the ground; no forward/backward distance is required.

cdc_milestone: Turns book pages, one at a time, when you read to her
question_text: Turns book pages one by one.
match_reason: Same turning book pages one at a time; no numeric rate observations are available for this question.

cdc_milestone: Talks well enough for others to understand, most of the time
question_text: Most people understand them when they speak.
match_reason: Same speech intelligibility to other people most of the time.

cdc_milestone: Strings items together, like large beads or macaroni
question_text: Inserts things like string into a small hole.
match_reason: Same threading action: inserting string through a hole, as in CDC's beads/macaroni. Kinedu does not require a counted chain of beads.

cdc_milestone: Puts on some clothes by himself, like loose pants or a jacket
question_text: Puts their pants on.
match_reason: Same putting on pants independently, one of CDC's explicit examples; neither requires fastening them.

cdc_milestone: Uses a fork
question_text: Feeds independently with a fork, using the whole hand.
match_reason: Same independent fork feeding; Kinedu's whole-hand grip adds no advanced utensil requirement.

cdc_milestone: Pretends to be something else during play (teacher, superhero, dog)
question_text: Engages in pretend play, like dressing up or acting like a firefighter.
match_reason: Same pretending to be a role/character during play, with firefighter versus teacher/superhero examples.

cdc_milestone: Comforts others who are hurt or sad, like hugging a crying friend
question_text: Shows empathy when they see a crying friend (e.g., will try to comfort them).
match_reason: Same active comforting of an upset person, including a crying friend; stronger than CDC's separate two-year noticing item.

cdc_milestone: Says sentences with four or more words
question_text: Talks in sentences with four to five words.
match_reason: Same minimum four-word sentence level; Kinedu describes four-to-five-word sentences.

cdc_milestone: Says some words from a song, story, or nursery rhyme
question_text: Sings a few words from a song.
match_reason: Same saying/singing a few words of a song; CDC's story/rhyme alternatives are not additional requirements.

cdc_milestone: Talks about at least one thing that happened during her day, like “I played soccer.”
question_text: Talks about their day.
match_reason: Same talking about events from one's day.

cdc_milestone: Names a few colors of items
question_text: Names two or more colors.
match_reason: Same expressive naming of multiple colors; Kinedu specifies two or more and CDC uses the imprecise a few.

cdc_milestone: Serves herself food or pours water, with adult supervision
question_text: Pours water from a pitcher into a cup with both hands.
match_reason: Same pouring water into a cup; Kinedu specifies a pitcher and two hands, CDC allows adult supervision.

cdc_milestone: Unbuttons some buttons
question_text: Can undo a big button on their clothes.
match_reason: Same unbuttoning action; Kinedu specifies a large button, one instance of CDC's some buttons without a specified size.
